Boston Dynamics redesigns Stretch Gen 2 for uptime and easier servicing

The new Stretch applies fleet experience to wiring, case handling and maintenance; actual throughput still depends on the load.

The Robot Report ↗6 November 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1Videos 3

A redesign informed by fleet use

Boston Dynamics detailed Stretch Gen 2 after roughly two and a half years of development, drawing on more than 100,000 operating hours and tens of millions of handled cases. Its stated ceiling of 1,000 cases per hour depends on weight and stacking conditions.

Simpler wiring and more selective gripping

Internal cabling was reduced by 81%, using automotive-style harnesses and connectors with Hyundai supply-chain support. Continuous-rotation joints reduce cable constraints. Individually sensed and controlled suction cups support multi-case picks followed by separate releases onto the conveyor.

Serviceability and operating conditions

A swerve-drive replacement is designed to take one hour rather than a full day, with standardized fasteners and improved diagnostics. The company also cites two-shift battery capacity and charging to 90% in 75 minutes. These are supplier figures to validate against each site’s cases and schedule.
